title: Charts & HUD content
summary: Pick what the HUD shows and how it looks.

blocks.title: Create, stow, send overboard and spyglass
blocks.body: Start from a built-in chart and Stow to create a custom copy aboard, or create a new chart. Send overboard removes custom charts while original presets remain. Spyglass uses the aboard now edit and real data; Stow commits it to the running HUD.

blocks.title: Text regions and icons
blocks.body: Tagline, title, primary/secondary text and the right-side value can mix literal text and variable tokens. Use the right suffix for units such as %, °C or GHz. Icons identify the content; the accent color sets the capsule and ring color.

blocks.title: Ring variable and range
blocks.body: The ring maps (value − minimum) over the configured range, clamped to 0–100%. Use a variable key or a numeric expression beginning with =. Set a sensible full-scale value for temperature, traffic or FPS. The range does not change the raw text reading.

blocks.title: Conditional colors
blocks.body: Add one variable/operator/threshold => color rule per line. Rules change the accent based on load, temperature and other values. Thresholds use the variable's original unit. Use valid color values; missing measurements are not treated as zero.

title: Variables, tokens & expressions
summary: Copy aboard from the library, then build readable HUD text.

blocks.title: Find and copy aboard a variable
blocks.body: Scout by name, key or category under Data Management → Variable Library. Select a variable to see its meaning, type, unit and formats. Copy aboard Variable Key is useful for rings and rules; Copy aboard Template includes braces for text fields.

blocks.title: Common token formats
blocks.body: Place the key in braces, followed by | and a display format. Use 0 for integers and 0.0 / 0.00 for fixed decimals. Literal text may surround tokens. Formatting changes display only.

blocks.title: Automatic units and pipelines
blocks.body: auto:1 chooses units based on the variable; avoid adding the same unit twice. Format pipelines run left to right and can transform numbers or shorten text. Use {= ...} for inline expressions, or start a ring expression with =.

blocks.title: Operators and conditions
blocks.body: Use +, -, *, /, % remainder, ^ power and parentheses. Comparisons support >, >=, <, <=, == and !=. Boolean operators include &&, ||, ! and and/or/not. Conditions use test ? aye : nay or if(test, aye, nay). ?? supplies a fallback for null/empty values.

blocks.title: Numeric function reference
blocks.body: Aggregates: min, max, avg and sum. Range/precision: clamp(value, min, max), round(value, digits), floor, ceil, abs and sign. Math: sqrt, pow, log, log10, exp, sin, cos and tan. percent(value, total) returns a percentage; between(value, min, max) tests an inclusive range.

blocks.title: Text, types and pipeline reference
blocks.body: Expression functions: len, contains, startswith, endswith, upper, lower and concat. Convert types with number, string or bool; inspect them with isnull, isempty and isnan. Token pipelines support upper/lower, zero-based sub:start:length, replace:old:new and math:add/sub/mul/div/round/floor/ceil/abs.

blocks.title: Capacity and time formats
blocks.body: bytes / speed add automatic byte-size or byte-rate units. kb:n, mb:n, gb:n and tb:n divide by powers of 1024 with n decimals; add the desired unit in the chart. duration / duration-long format seconds. Date/time fields support time:<date format>; time:relative formats relative time or duration.

blocks.title: Hardware variables and legacy keys
blocks.body: Once equivalent hardware fields are discovered, duplicate legacy entries leave the library while existing charts keep working. New keys identify a specific vessel and sensor. Highest/average summaries have different meanings and remain separate. -- means nay valid value is currently available.

blocks.title: DeepSeek balance and peak periods
blocks.body: Enter a DeepSeek API key under Data Management → Data Source Configuration, then Stow & Hoist. Keys are encrypted for the aboard now Android user and may need re-entry for another account or machine. Peak portholes use Beijing time and the Chinese holiday calendar; weekend make-up workdays remain off-peak.

blocks.title: Configure HTTP / JSON
blocks.body:
Enter an HTTP/HTTPS GET URL that returns JSON and name the source.
Map response paths such as data.value or players[0].name to variable names.
Set required headers and take another sighting seconds, bring aboard the source, then Stow & Hoist.
Find custom.<source>.<variable> in the library and use it in a chart.

blocks.title: Copyable JSON structure
blocks.body: This structure is ashore. Replace the URL with yer real endpoint, adjust paths to the response and set aboard to true when ready. ${env:MY_API_KEY} reads a process environment variable instead of putting a secret directly in JSON.

blocks.title: Status, cache and errors
blocks.body: Use custom.<source>.status / trouble ahead for source state and failures. The take another sighting interval controls caching, even with faster global sampling. For 401/403, check authentication and access. JSON paths must match the actual response structure.

blocks.title: Build a carousel queue
blocks.body: Add charts to the queue and use Move Up/Down to order them. Removing from the queue does not send overboard the chart. Automatic cycling advances at the configured interval. An empty queue uses the active chart; a single-item queue cannot switch to a different item.

blocks.title: Three cycle animations
blocks.body: Simple shortens the presentation; Full uses the shipshape summon. Roll Up moves icons, values and the ring inside a persistent capsule while retaining its porthole and layer. Roll applies to persistent switches; initial and transient presentations keep their normal show/retract lifecycle. DeepSeek peak transitions keep Full animation.

blocks.title: Click a persistent HUD to switch
blocks.body: Bring aboard click cycling to advance through the queue even with automatic cycling off. Each HUD advances its own instance and resets its cycle timer. Transparent areas remain click-through. Empty or single-item queues do not switch.
